chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'Be patient with the world, for it is but a moment. So whatever of it has passed, you will find neither pain nor joy for it; and whatever has not yet come, you do not know what it is. And it is only your moment which you are in now, so be patient in it upon the obedience of Allah, and be patient in it from the disobedience of Allah.'

key_terms.سَاعَةٌ: A moment, a short period of time

ai.seo_question: How should one practice patience in relation to the transient nature of the world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) advises believers to exercise patience with the transient nature of the world, which is merely a single moment. One should not dwell on the past which brings neither pain nor joy, nor worry about the unknown future, but rather focus on the present moment by obeying Allah and avoiding His disobedience. This teaching, found in al-Kafi, emphasizes the concept of 'present-moment mindfulness' in Shia spirituality, urging believers to anchor their worship and moral conduct in the immediate 'now' as the only tangible reality.
